messages:
ella: Heads-up — CS escalation from Acme Analytics. They hit intermittent 429s starting ~2026-03-10T14:02Z and also reported a ~2M token billing spike in the same window. They say requests originate from their reverse proxy (various client IPs) but are all under the same org; they expect project-level quotas to apply (multiple projects/keys), not a single org-level cap. They attached a sample request/response.

ella: Sample response from our API they pasted:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 14:03:15 GMT
Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limit_exceeded",
    "scope": "org",
    "message": "org quota exceeded",
    "retry_after": 30
  }
}
```

ella: They also included the original request headers — note the proxy-supplied X-Forwarded-For list and the bearer token for project A:
```
Authorization: Bearer sk-projectA-xxxx
X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.10, 198.51.100.11
User-Agent: acme-proxy/1.2
```

devin: Thanks, tagging @oliver. Can you paste the request_id (req_0a1b2c3d) trace log? I want to see which quota rule matched and whether attribution was API-key or IP-based. Also need the edge logs for the 14:02–14:10 window.

oliver: grabbing logs now. Quick summary while I search: our quota evaluation pipeline historically checks in this order: API key -> project -> org -> IP-burst fallback. The IP-burst path was implemented to allow short bursts from public endpoints when no key is present. I'm seeing something weird in the traces — when X-Forwarded-For header is present, the IP-burst check runs _before_ the API key attribution in the edge cache path. That means if an org-level IP burst has been consumed, subsequent requests still carry an API key but are being short-circuited and tagged as org-level 429s.

oliver: log excerpt for req_0a1b2c3d (edge log):
```
2026-03-10T14:03:15Z edge-1 INFO request_id=req_0a1b2c3d src=198.51.100.10 xfwd=\"198.51.100.10, 203.0.113.5\" auth=sk-projectA-xxxx step=ip_burst_check result=limit_hit scope=org
2026-03-10T14:03:15Z edge-1 DEBUG quota_eval: short_circuit=true matched_rule=ip_burst window=60s consumed=12000 tokens
2026-03-10T14:03:15Z qm INFO attribution=org org_id=org_123 project_id=null api_key=null
```

oliver: Notice api_key=null in the attribution line — that's the bug. We later see the auth token parsed correctly in the auth middleware, but because ip_burst_check set short_circuit on the fast-path we never wired the api key through to the quota metering call.

kelly: That matches a code path I audited last week. There was a micro-optimisation (cache hit fast-path) added to fix latency for unauthenticated public calls; looks like the path assumed auth is absent if X-Forwarded-For exists. Edge case: reverse proxies that preserve X-Forwarded-For will hit that path even when they include Authorization header.

devin: Can you reproduce locally? Suggest we run a small loop of requests that include both Authorization and X-Forwarded-For and compare attribution headers in the edge trace. If we can reproduce we can craft a minimal failing test for the patch.

oliver: Repro steps (I ran them against staging edge-2):
1) curl -i -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-projectA-TEST\" \\
  -H \"X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.10\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-small\",\"input\":\"hi\"}'
2) Repeat 80 times in quick succession (we hit our IP-burst window).
3) Observe 429s with JSON body scope=org and edge logs showing api_key=null.

oliver: Minimal reproducer attached in gist (internal) and I filed a failing unit test in the edge router repo. Repro is deterministic if X-Forwarded-For present.

billing-bot: Billing alert: unusual spike detected for org_123 — +2,045,312 tokens billed between 2026-03-10T14:00Z and 2026-03-10T16:00Z. Invoice flagged. (auto-note)

ella: Customer is asking for credits and wants to know whether tokens were charged to org vs project. They clearly expected project-level quotas for their projectA key. They also say other projects under same org were unaffected — so the billing attribution they see in their console is confusing.

devin: Short-term mitigation: can we temporarily disable IP-burst short-circuit on prod edge? That will increase a tiny bit of latency for unauth requests but will correctly attribute to API keys. If we push that toggle it should stop new misattributions.

oliver: I pushed a toggle to staging and ran the same reproducer — attribution shows project_id=projectA and api_key=sk-projectA-TEST, 429s (if any) are applied to the project quota not org. I'll prepare a hotfix PR to change the order: always parse & attach auth info before evaluating the ip_burst fast-path. Patch also includes an additional guard: if auth header present, do not short-circuit based on IP.

kelly: From infra side, prepping a runbook to flip the toggle in prod and roll back if we see latency regressions. Also adding a tracing tag to all quota hits so we can quickly filter affected requests.

ella: Customer-facing plan: offer immediate token credit for the 2M tokens charged to org, explain root cause and that we will backfill project-level attribution in billing so their project usage/limits reflect reality. Can we confirm the exact token count we will credit per project? We need a mapping.

oliver: I'll generate an attribution map using edge logs (request_id -> api_key resolved post-patch). We can reprocess raw logs for that 2-hour window to map requests to project keys where possible. If a request truly had no Authorization on record, it'll remain org-attributed and we won't credit that.

devin: Next steps / timeline
- hotfix toggle to prod (devin / edge oncall) — 30m window for rollout; monitor latency + error rate
- run backfill attribution job (oliver) — estimate 2 hours for 48h of logs
- billing credit issuance (billing team + ella) — coordinate message
- postmortem and retrospective (kelly) — include recommendations: ensure auth parsed before fast-path, add unit tests, and add e2e with X-Forwarded-For present.

ella: I'll draft the customer communication and ask CS to hold until hotfix verified. Thanks all — tagging @devin @oliver for the immediate rollout. :thumbsup:
